thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: sustained p95 latency spike on /v1/stream and rising 5xx rate across US-WEST2. Autoretry suppression kicked in. paging @anya @matt @jordan
anya: grabbing logs, looks like SSE client disconnects spiking and many worker containers hitting high CPU and blocked on evicting KV cache
matt: on it, attaching profiler now. Are we seeing a correlated surge in prefix reuse? any recent rollout?
meera: no prod model rollouts in the last 2h. Network egress looks normal. Our telemetry shows concurrent open connections for streaming up ~3.6x baseline in the last 15m
anya: repro of metric: from grafana - stream_conn_count_usw2 = 3.6x, stream_5xx_rate = 2.1%, p95_token_latency = 850ms, non-streaming p95 = 220ms
sre-rotation: can we temporarily reduce streaming load while we stabilize? propose targeted mitigation: disable server-push (SSE/ws) for non-enterprise customers and enable short-poll fallback for them
matt: agree with targeted approach. full global disable is heavy; do per-plan feature-flag flip for "streaming_push" via config API. that'll avoid progressive degradation for premium/enterprise
meera: support plan mapping: free/standard = feature-flag group "tier:standard", enterprise/premium = "tier:enterprise". We can flip for tier:standard in us-west2 and us-east1 first. Command:

```
# flip flag for standard tier in us-west2
curl -X POST "https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/streaming_push/toggle" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"enabled":false,"scope":{"tier":"standard","region":"us-west2"}}'
```

support-ops: are we prepared to return HTTP 200 with streaming-disabled hint so SDKs fallback gracefully? we need to update gateway behaviour
anya: yes, gateway has a short-circuit code path: if feature-flag off, it responds normal generation but with streaming=false and includes header X-Stream-Disabled: reason=mitigation. I'll patch config and rollout in stages
incident-bot: Deployment pipeline trigger: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full region
matt: doing canary now for us-west2 standard tier. patching flag + rolling gateway config on canary subset (pods 3-4). watching metrics
jordan: I'll open a support post template just in case customers hit it. draft:
"We temporarily disabled streaming responses in your region to stabilize performance. You will receive full-generation responses via polling. We expect service restoration within 1 hour. Contact support if you need priority access."
support-ops: noted, will have canned response ready and update statuspage if mitigation lasts >15m
anya: canary results after 3m: stream_conn_count down 42% on canary nodes, p95_token_latency for affected requests dropped from 850ms to 260ms on those nodes, 5xx rate dropped from 2.1% to 0.3%
meera: good signal. proceed to 10% -> 50% across us-west2. I'll also increase token rate limiter for all customers by +15% temporarily to throttle bursts (quota key: api:burst:region:us-west2). Command to set redis token bucket:

```
# increase burst window
redis-cli -h redis-prod us-west2 HSET token_bucket:api:burst rate "1.15"
```

matt: 10% -> 50% rolled. overall p95 now approx 310ms region-wide vs 850ms earlier. CPU on workers still elevated but within safe bounds. We're seeing some SDKs log reconnects; support template will help
sre-rotation: any customers on premium who need stream preserved? we kept tier:enterprise untouched but some premium customers are mapped to custom flags
meera: doing a quick query to ensure no enterprise customers covered by the standard flag. 2 accounts found (acct-9192, acct-7281) - moving them to enterprise-override
matt: note: some experiments rely on long-lived streaming sessions for token-cost accounting. ops to ensure usage meters don't double-count when clients fall back to polling
support-ops: updated status page: "Degraded — We have temporarily disabled server-push streaming for standard-tier customers in US regions to reduce latency and error rates. We are monitoring."
incident-bot: Pager silence scheduled for on-call to avoid noisy repeats; critical escalations still enabled
anya: small regression: after 50% rollout, we saw an unexpected spike in queued polling requests causing memory pressure in the gateway. mitigation: add short backoff and small batching window on polling endpoints. patch pushed as hotfix
matt: hotfix applied to polling path (batch window = 200ms, max batch size = 8). watching for memory stabilisation
jordan: customer comms ready. support-ops to send proactive messages to accounts with active streaming sessions > 30m
support-ops: sent proactive messages to top 50 affected accounts with instructions and apology + optional temporary enterprise uplift link
meera: metrics 12m after full regional flip: p95_token_latency = 280ms, 5xx_rate = 0.35%, stream_conn_count down 70% overall. memory pressure resolved. CPU trending down
anya: next steps: 1) keep streaming off for standard tier until sustained stability for 1h 2) continue monitoring for regressions 3) postmortem once incident closed
sre-rotation: handing off monitoring to @jordan for the next 2h window. checklist for handoff:
- confirm p95_token_latency < 350ms for 15m
- 5xx_rate < 0.5% for 15m
- no memory or OOM events in gateway
- notify eng-runtime if any new spikes
jordan: acknowledged. I'll monitor dashboards and update every 20m. if we sustain for 1h we'll begin staged re-enable plan: re-enable streaming for standard-tier in canary nodes first and observe for 30m
matt: log note for postmortem: probable root cause interplay between excessive long-lived streaming connections + KV cache eviction latencies leading to head-of-line blocking on token emission. mitigation set: feature-flag gating, rate-limit tweaks, polling batching.
meera: filing incident ticket with timeline and all commands executed + diff of config flips
anya: good job team. reactions: :thumbsup: :coffee:
incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, start_ts=2030012345, mitigation_action=targeted_streaming_disable, owners=[matt,anya,jordan], followup=postmortem
jordan: handing off to next on-call. I'll post updates if thresholds cross. leaving the thread open for final close when PRs and postmortem are linked.
support-ops: closing customer comm loop after final restore message. will attach sent templates to incident ticket
matt: adding short note: when re-enabling, plan to increase canary observation to 30m and keep polling batching in place for 1h
jordan: last check before handoff: p95=295ms, 5xx=0.31%, stream_conn_count steady. handing off now. :white_check_mark:
